docs.title: Home
docs.text:
CLI-FIRST AI RESEARCH ASSISTANT One Command. Search. Reason. Answer.

Zuni brings AI-assisted research to your terminal. Ask a question, let the model use web tools when needed, and get a concise answer with sources you can inspect.

Get Started → View on GitHub zuni 
$ zuni ask "What is quantum computing?"

→ web_search: quantum computing
→ extract_markdown: https://...

Quantum computing uses quantum-mechanical phenomena
to process information differently from classical
computers. [1]

Sources
[1] Source title
    https://...
WHY ZUNI Research without leavingthe terminal.

Zuni combines an OpenAI-compatible LLM client with a small tool-calling agent and web research tools.

⚡ One Command

Ask a question from the terminal and let Zuni manage the research workflow.

⌕ Web Research

Search DuckDuckGo and read selected pages when a question needs factual or current information.

◈ Grounded Answers

Sources are numbered and can be cited inline, making it easier to inspect the material behind an answer.

THE FLOW From question to answer,through tools. 01 Ask

Write your question.

→ 02 Research

The model can call search and page-reading tools.

→ 03 Answer

Zuni returns a Markdown response with source references.

GET STARTED OPEN SOURCE Built in the open.

Zuni is an evolving open-source project. Explore the code, follow the roadmap, or contribute to its development.

GitHub ↗ START EXPLORING Open your terminal.

Ask the question. Let Zuni handle the research.

Get Started →

docs.title: Install and meet Zuni in one command.
docs.text:
uv tool install ssannssarr.zuni

Then ask:

zuni ask "Explain how DNS works"

Research tools are available by default. To send the question directly to the model:

zuni ask --no-search "Explain recursion"

Read the installation guide →

docs.title: What is Zuni?
docs.text: Zuni is a command-line AI research assistant. It sends questions to an OpenAI-compatible model and can use web-search tools to gather information before producing an answer.

docs.title: Does Zuni search the web?
docs.text:
Yes. Web research is enabled by default for zuni ask. The model can call web_search to search DuckDuckGo and extract_markdown to read a selected public page.

Use --no-search when you want to bypass the research workflow.

docs.title: Does every model support tool calling?
docs.text:
No. Tool calling depends on the model and provider.

If the first tool-enabled request fails, Zuni falls back to a simpler workflow:

search the web → collect sources → send the sources to the model

docs.title: Is Zuni free?
docs.text: The Zuni software is open source under the MIT License. Your model provider may charge for API usage, depending on the provider and model you choose.

docs.title: Which providers work?
docs.text:
Zuni targets providers that expose an OpenAI-compatible POST /chat/completions endpoint.

Tool calling also requires support for the tools request format.

docs.title: Does Zuni store my questions?
docs.text:
Zuni stores configuration locally and does not implement a server-side conversation database.

Requests sent to hosted model or web services are handled according to those services' own privacy policies.

docs.title: Where is my API key stored?
docs.text:
By default, a key entered through zuni config is stored at:

~/.config/zuni/config.json

You can override it with ZUNI_API_KEY.

Protect the configuration file and never commit it to Git.

docs.title: Can I use a local model?
docs.text:
Yes, if the local model server exposes an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint.

For example:

http://localhost:11434/v1

Use --no-search if you do not want Zuni to access the web.

docs.title: Can I use Zuni offline?
docs.text:
The direct LLM path can work without internet access when the configured model server is reachable locally.

Web research requires network access.

docs.title: How does citation work?
docs.text:
Zuni assigns numbers to collected sources:

[1] First source
[2] Second source

The model is instructed to use those numbers for inline citations. Zuni then prints the corresponding source URLs below the answer.

docs.title: How do I control the number of search results?
docs.text:
Use the -n or --results option:

zuni ask -n 3 "Your question"

The allowed range is 1 to 10, with 5 as the default.

docs.title: How do I change the model?
docs.text:
Run:

zuni config

You can also edit:

~/.config/zuni/config.json

The base URL can be overridden with ZUNI_BASE_URL.

docs.title: Where can I contribute?
docs.text: See Contributing for the development workflow and contribution guidelines.

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text:
Zuni is developing from a small command-line question-answering tool into a compact terminal research assistant.

This roadmap describes direction rather than a fixed release schedule. Items can change as the project evolves.

docs.title: Available now
docs.text:
• One-command questions with zuni ask
  • Interactive configuration with zuni config
  • OpenAI-compatible chat-completions support
  • Markdown rendering in the terminal
  • Asynchronous HTTP requests
  • Retry handling for temporary LLM API failures
  • Tool-calling agent
  • DuckDuckGo web search
  • Web-page extraction to Markdown
  • Numbered source tracking and citations
  • Fallback search flow for models without tool calling
  • Direct-answer mode with --no-search
  • First PyPI release (0.1.0)

docs.title: In progress
docs.text:
• Stronger validation of model-generated tool calls
  • More robust URL and redirect safety
  • Automated tests for configuration, tools, citations, and the agent loop
  • Expanded documentation and API reference

docs.title: Planned
docs.text:
• Streaming responses
  • Conversation mode
  • Reading input from stdin
  • Multiple saved configuration profiles
  • Continuous integration

docs.title: Ideas
docs.text:
• Shell completions
  • JSON and other structured output formats
  • Additional research tools
  • Local and offline-first workflows
  • More provider-specific configuration options

Note

The roadmap is intentionally flexible. Features may move, change, or be removed as Zuni's design develops.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Contributions are welcome in code, documentation, bug fixes, testing, and project ideas.

docs.title: Development setup
docs.text:
Clone the repository and install its development dependencies:

git clone https://github.com/ssannssarr/Zuni.git
cd Zuni
uv sync
uv run zuni --help

For a global editable installation:

uv tool install --editable .

docs.title: Preview the documentation
docs.text:
Start the local MkDocs server:

uv run mkdocs serve

Open the local address shown by MkDocs and check both the homepage and regular documentation pages.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
A typical contribution looks like this:

  1. Fork the repository.
  2. Create a focused branch.
  3. Make the change.
  4. Run the relevant commands locally.
  5. Update documentation when behavior changes.
  6. Commit the change with a clear message.
  7. Push the branch and open a pull request.

For example:

git checkout -b feature/my-change

docs.title: Commit messages
docs.text:
Keep commit messages short and descriptive:

feat: add streaming responses
fix: handle missing config file
docs: expand installation guide
refactor: simplify tool dispatch
Prefix Use for feat New features fix Bug fixes docs Documentation changes refactor Internal restructuring

docs.title: Code guidelines
docs.text:
• Keep functions focused and easy to follow.
  • Use type hints where practical.
  • Prefer asynchronous APIs for network operations.
  • Keep user-facing errors clear and actionable.
  • Never commit API keys or local configuration files.
  • Treat model-controlled network access as untrusted input.

docs.title: Tool and web-search changes
docs.text:
When modifying a tool:

  • keep its schema and implementation in sync
  • validate required arguments
  • preserve useful error messages
  • avoid exposing secrets in tool output
  • consider URL and redirect safety
  • update the architecture documentation when behavior changes

docs.title: Documentation guidelines
docs.text:
Documentation should describe the current implementation.

  • Keep examples runnable.
  • Prefer short sections and clear headings.
  • Explain behavior before implementation details.
  • Update links when pages move.
  • Keep architecture documentation synchronized with the code.
  • Avoid presenting planned features as if they already exist.

docs.title: Areas for contribution
docs.text:
Some useful areas include:

  • agent and tool tests
  • configuration handling
  • URL safety
  • error handling
  • documentation
  • CI
  • packaging

docs.title: Reporting a bug
docs.text:
When opening an issue, include:

  • the command you ran
  • the complete error output
  • your OS and Python version
  • your Zuni version or commit
  • relevant configuration with secrets removed

Warning

Never include API keys, access tokens, or private configuration values in an issue.

docs.title: License
docs.text: By contributing, you agree that your contribution is released under the project's MIT License.

docs.text: Path Responsibility src/zuni/cli.py CLI commands, execution flow, and terminal output src/zuni/agent.py Tool-calling loop src/zuni/errors.py Zuni exception types src/zuni/llm/config.py Configuration loading and saving src/zuni/llm/llm.py OpenAI-compatible API client src/zuni/prompts/prompt.py Prompt loading src/zuni/prompts/system.md Base system prompt src/zuni/search/search.py HTTP requests and DuckDuckGo parsing src/zuni/tools/schema.py Tool definitions sent to the model src/zuni/tools/toolbox.py Tool dispatch and source tracking src/zuni/tools/web_search.py Search and page enrichment src/zuni/tools/extract_markdown.py HTML-to-Markdown extraction

docs.title: Packaging
docs.text:
pyproject.toml contains the package metadata, runtime dependencies, Python requirement, and console-script entry point:

[project.scripts]
zuni = "zuni.cli:main"

The repository uses Python 3.14 for development, while the package metadata supports Python 3.11 and newer.

docs.title: Changing a command
docs.text:
When adding or changing a command:

  1. Update src/zuni/cli.py.
  2. Test it with uv run zuni ....
  3. Update Commands.
  4. Update the architecture page if the execution flow changes.

docs.title: Adding a tool
docs.text:
A tool has three main parts:

  1. A schema in src/zuni/tools/schema.py.
  2. Dispatch logic in src/zuni/tools/toolbox.py.
  3. The implementation in the relevant search or tool module.

The schema name and dispatcher name must remain consistent.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
Preview the documentation locally with:

uv run mkdocs serve

When code behavior changes, update the corresponding documentation page in the same change whenever practical.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Zuni connects to an OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions endpoint. The default base URL is OpenRouter when no other base URL is configured.

docs.title: Interactive setup
docs.text:
The simplest way to configure Zuni is:

zuni config

You will be asked for three values:

Prompt Purpose Example API key Credential used to access the model API sk-or-v1-... Model ID Model identifier accepted by the provider openrouter/free Base URL API root, without /chat/completions https://openrouter.ai/api/v1

The values are saved to:

~/.config/zuni/config.json

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
A typical configuration looks like this:

{
    "API_KEY": "your-api-key",
    "MODEL": "openrouter/free",
    "BASE_URL": "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"
}

Keep this file private because it can contain your API key.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Purpose ZUNI_API_KEY Overrides API_KEY from the config file ZUNI_BASE_URL Overrides BASE_URL from the config file Bash / ZshFishPowerShell 
export ZUNI_API_KEY="your-api-key"
export ZUNI_BASE_URL="https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"

set -Ux ZUNI_API_KEY "your-api-key"
set -Ux ZUNI_BASE_URL "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"

$env:ZUNI_API_KEY = "your-api-key"
$env:ZUNI_BASE_URL = "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"

docs.title: API key
docs.text:
1. ZUNI_API_KEY
  2. API_KEY in config.json
  3. Error

docs.title: Model
docs.text:
1. MODEL in config.json
  2. openrouter/free

docs.title: Base URL
docs.text:
1. ZUNI_BASE_URL
  2. BASE_URL in config.json
  3. The default URL in the LLM client

docs.title: Provider examples
docs.text:
OpenRouterOpenAILocal Ollama 
Base URL: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
Model ID: openrouter/free

Base URL: https://api.openai.com/v1
Model ID: <your-model>

Zuni can work with providers that implement the OpenAI-compatible POST /chat/completions interface. Tool calling also requires support for the tools request format.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
Warning

Never commit your API key or config.json to Git. If an API key is exposed, revoke it through the provider and create a replacement.

On Linux, macOS, and Termux, you can restrict access to the configuration file:

chmod 600 ~/.config/zuni/config.json

docs.title: Reset configuration
docs.text:
Remove the configuration file and run setup again:

rm ~/.config/zuni/config.json
zuni config

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Get Zuni installed and ready to use from your terminal.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Requirement Version Notes Python 3.11+ Minimum version supported by the package uv Latest Recommended for installation and project management API key Provider-dependent Required when using a hosted model API Internet access Required for web research Not required for a local model used without web tools

The repository currently uses Python 3.14 for development through .python-version.

docs.title: Install uv
docs.text:
Linux / macOSWindows (PowerShell)pip 
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"

pip install uv

Verify the installation:

uv --version

docs.title: Install Zuni
docs.text:
Zuni is published on PyPI. Install the latest release with:

uv tool install ssannssarr.zuni

Then verify the command:

zuni --help

You should see the ask and config commands.

Tip

If you want to install a specific release, append the version, for example uv tool install ssannssarr.zuni==0.1.0.

docs.title: Configure Zuni
docs.text:
Run:

zuni config

Zuni will ask for your API key, model ID, and base URL. See Configuration for details.

docs.title: Install from source
docs.text:
For development or local changes:

git clone https://github.com/ssannssarr/Zuni.git
cd Zuni
uv sync
uv run zuni --help

Tip

Use uv tool install --editable . from the repository if you want a global zuni command that follows your local source changes.

docs.title: Update
docs.text:
For a PyPI installation:

uv tool upgrade ssannssarr.zuni

For a source checkout:

git pull
uv sync

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
Remove the tool installation with:

uv tool uninstall ssannssarr.zuni

If you also want to remove the local configuration:

rm -rf ~/.config/zuni

docs.title: If the command is not found
docs.text:
Refresh uv's shell integration:

uv tool update-shell

Restart your terminal and try again. If the problem continues, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Zuni is an asynchronous CLI built around four main pieces: an OpenAI-compatible LLM client, a small tool-calling agent, web research tools, and a terminal interface.

docs.title: High-level flow
docs.text:
zuni ask
   │
   ▼
 cli.py
   │
   ├── --no-search ──► LLM ──► Markdown
   │
   └── research mode
          │
          ▼
       Agent loop
          │
      ┌───┴───────────┐
      ▼               ▼
 web_search     extract_markdown
      │               │
      └───────┬───────┘
              ▼
          tool results
              │
              ▼
             LLM
              │
              ▼
       Markdown + sources

The important idea is simple: the model decides when it needs a tool, Zuni executes that tool, and the result is returned to the model as part of the conversation.

docs.title: cli.py
docs.text: The CLI defines the commands and coordinates each request. It loads configuration and prompts, creates the LLM client and Toolbox, selects direct or research mode, handles the tool-calling fallback, renders Markdown, and prints sources.

docs.title: agent.py
docs.text:
run_agent() implements the tool-calling loop:

LLM request
    ↓
assistant message
    ↓
tool calls?
  ├─ no → final answer
  └─ yes
       ↓
Toolbox.run(...)
       ↓
tool result added to chat
       ↓
LLM request again

The current agent allows up to four tool-call rounds by default. If the limit is reached, Zuni asks the model to answer using the information collected so far.

If the first tool-enabled request is rejected, the CLI treats it as a possible tool-support issue and uses the search-first fallback.

docs.title: llm/llm.py
docs.text:
The LLM class builds OpenAI-compatible chat-completion requests. It can attach tool definitions, sends requests asynchronously with httpx, retries temporary failures, maps API errors, and extracts assistant messages.

Requests are sent to:

{BASE_URL}/chat/completions

docs.title: llm/config.py
docs.text:
This module loads and saves Zuni's configuration at:

~/.config/zuni/config.json

It resolves the API key, model, and base URL from the configuration file and supported environment variables.

docs.title: tools/schema.py
docs.text:
This module defines the tool schemas sent to the model.

Tool Purpose web_search Search DuckDuckGo and return source material extract_markdown Fetch a public page and extract readable Markdown

docs.title: tools/toolbox.py
docs.text: Toolbox connects model tool calls to their Python implementations. It parses arguments, dispatches tools, tracks sources, assigns source numbers, and turns tool failures into results the model can understand.

docs.title: tools/web_search.py
docs.text: The web-search tool searches DuckDuckGo and can fetch selected result pages to enrich the returned source material. Page downloads are performed concurrently.

docs.title: search/search.py
docs.text: This module provides lower-level HTTP requests, DuckDuckGo parsing, and URL checks used before page fetching.

docs.title: tools/extract_markdown.py
docs.text: This module removes common HTML noise such as scripts, navigation, forms, and iframes, then extracts the most relevant page content and converts it to Markdown.

docs.title: Sources and citations
docs.text:
Zuni represents a source as:

Source(index, title, url, content)

Toolbox owns the source list. A source receives a number when it is first registered. Repeated URLs reuse the existing source number.

The final model response can contain citations such as [1] and [2]. The CLI reads those references and prints the matching source URLs below the answer.

docs.title: Direct mode
docs.text:
Use:

zuni ask --no-search "Explain recursion"

Direct mode skips the agent and web tools:

CLI → system prompt + question → LLM → Markdown

docs.title: Design goals
docs.text:
• CLI first: keep the interface small and terminal-friendly.
  • Async: use asynchronous APIs for network operations.
  • Provider neutral: work with the common OpenAI-compatible chat-completions format.
  • Tool based: keep web capabilities behind explicit model-callable tools.
  • Grounded: retain source information so answers can reference retrieved material.
  • Small core: keep the agent and tool layer understandable.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Zuni keeps its command-line interface small:

zuni [COMMAND] [ARGUMENTS]
Command Purpose zuni ask Ask a question, with optional web research zuni config Configure the API key, model, and base URL zuni --help Show command help

docs.title: zuni ask
docs.text:
Ask a question directly from your terminal:

zuni ask "Explain how DNS works"

Web research is enabled by default. The model can choose to use Zuni's available tools before producing the answer.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: zuni ask [OPTIONS] PROMPT...

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Option Description --no-search Skip the agent and tools and ask the model directly -n, --results INTEGER Maximum number of search results, from 1 to 10; default: 5

If the prompt contains multiple shell arguments, Zuni joins them into one question.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
ResearchDirect modelChoose result count 
zuni ask "What are the latest changes in Python?"
zuni ask "Compare HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2"

zuni ask --no-search "Explain recursion"
zuni ask --no-search "Write a Python function that reverses a string"

zuni ask -n 3 "What is quantum computing?"
zuni ask --results 8 "Compare current Linux distributions"

docs.title: Research flow
docs.text:
For a normal research request:

  1. Zuni loads the configuration and system prompt.
  2. The LLM receives the question and available tool definitions.
  3. The model can call web_search.
  4. Zuni runs the requested tool and returns its result to the model.
  5. The model can call extract_markdown when it needs to read a page.
  6. The agent repeats the tool loop until the model answers or the step limit is reached.
  7. Zuni renders the answer as Markdown.
  8. Zuni prints the relevant sources below the answer.

If the selected model cannot use tool calling, Zuni switches to a simpler search-first flow: it collects web results and sends them to the model in a normal request.

docs.title: Sources and citations
docs.text:
Web sources are assigned numbers:

[1] Source title
URL: https://example.com/...

[2] Another source
URL: https://example.org/...

The model is instructed to cite these numbers inline, for example [1]. Zuni then prints the corresponding source URLs below the answer.

docs.title: Shell quoting
docs.text:
Quote prompts when they contain shell characters such as $:

zuni ask 'What does $PATH do?'
zuni ask "What is Python's GIL?"

docs.title: Save an answer
docs.text:
Redirect the terminal output to a file:

zuni ask "List five Linux commands" > answer.txt

Rich terminal formatting is not preserved in the redirected output.

docs.title: Alias
docs.text:
You can create a short shell alias:

alias z='zuni ask'
z "What is a mutex?"

docs.title: zuni config
docs.text:
Run the interactive configuration command:

zuni config

It asks for the API key, model ID, and base URL. See Configuration for the details.

docs.title: Help
docs.text:
Use the built-in help whenever you need the exact command syntax:

zuni --help
zuni ask --help
zuni config --help

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: This page covers common installation, configuration, network, and model issues.

docs.title: zuni: command not found
docs.text:
Refresh uv's shell integration:

uv tool update-shell

Restart your terminal and try again.

docs.title: Configuration file errors
docs.text:
If Zuni reports that the configuration file does not exist, run:

zuni config

The default configuration path is:

~/.config/zuni/config.json

docs.title: API key errors
docs.text:
You can provide the key through the environment:

export ZUNI_API_KEY="your-api-key"

Or run zuni config.

The current implementation reads ZUNI_API_KEY; it does not use OPENROUTER_API_KEY automatically.

docs.title: Authentication errors
docs.text:
For HTTP 401 or 403 responses, check:

  • the API key
  • the provider
  • the model ID
  • whether the account has access to the selected model

docs.title: Model or provider errors
docs.text:
Zuni sends requests to:

{BASE_URL}/chat/completions

Check MODEL and BASE_URL in your configuration and make sure the provider exposes the expected OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

docs.title: Rate limits
docs.text: The LLM client retries temporary failures, including HTTP 429 and common 5xx responses. If the provider continues returning errors, wait and try again or select another model.

docs.title: Connection or timeout errors
docs.text:
Check your:

  • internet connection
  • base URL
  • provider availability
  • firewall or network restrictions
  • VPN configuration

The LLM client currently uses a 60-second default timeout and retries temporary failures.

docs.title: Web search fails
docs.text:
DuckDuckGo can temporarily limit automated requests. If web search fails, Zuni can continue without results or use its search-first fallback when the selected model cannot use tools.

For questions that do not require web research:

zuni ask --no-search "Explain recursion"

docs.title: The model does not support tools
docs.text:
Tool calling is not available from every OpenAI-compatible model or provider.

When the first tool-enabled request fails, Zuni falls back to:

web search → collect sources → normal LLM request

This fallback is simpler than the normal agent workflow, but it still gives the model the collected source material.

docs.title: Answers have no citations
docs.text:
Citations depend on the model using the source numbers provided by Zuni.

If an answer has no citations:

  1. Check that web research actually ran.
  2. Look at the source list printed below the answer.
  3. Check whether the answer contains source references such as [1].

Zuni only displays citation numbers that correspond to collected sources.

docs.title: A page cannot be fetched
docs.text:
Zuni rejects obvious local, private, or non-HTTP(S) targets when reading model-selected URLs.

A public page can still fail to load because of:

  • anti-bot protection
  • authentication requirements
  • redirects
  • network errors
  • unusual or unsupported HTML

docs.title: Python version
docs.text:
The package supports Python 3.11+. The repository currently uses Python 3.14 for development.

Check your version with:

python --version

docs.title: Debug mode
docs.text:
Set ZUNI_DEBUG to allow unexpected exceptions to propagate:

ZUNI_DEBUG=1 zuni ask "your question"

Use this when you need a traceback for debugging.

docs.title: Still stuck?
docs.text:
Open an issue with:

  • the command you ran
  • the complete error output
  • your OS and Python version
  • your Zuni version or commit
  • relevant configuration with secrets removed

Never include an API key or access token.
